citation: A Full Three-Dimensional GPU-Accelerated Model for Deep Borehole Heat Exchangers (DBHEs) Enabling Simulation of Well Arrays. 51st Workshop on Geothermal Reservoir Engineering, 2026.
description: Collin Wittenstein develops GeothermalWells.jl for simulating single deep-borehole heat exchangers and well arrays. Version 0.3.1 is archived on Zenodo, with source and documentation free under the MIT licence. The Julia package defines materials, boreholes, adaptive grids and inlet conditions, then solves the thermal response using CPU or GPU backends. Documentation requires Julia 1.12 or newer and provides working examples beyond the illustrative README pseudocode. The model can compare well layouts and long-term thermal interference in geothermal infrastructure design. Related G6 records model-deep-borehole-array-thesis-experiments and data-deep-borehole-heat-array-temperature-benchmarks provide specific experiment configurations and results. Geographic applicability depends on user-supplied geology and operating conditions. The project warns of active development and possible breaking changes. Benchmark agreement and backend performance are provider claims, with site calibration and model uncertainty still requiring assessment. No package was installed or simulation executed.
